paper_title: Towards Predicting Any Human Trajectory In Context
caption: Performance of random example selection and the proposed STES at varying numbers of in-context examples.

model_annotations.English: The plot illustrates the performance of two methods—ST-ES (proposed method) and Random example selection—measured by the minADE₂₀ metric, as the number of in-context examples varies from 0 to 8. The x-axis represents the "Number of Examples," scaled linearly from 0 to 8 with integer tick marks at regular intervals of 1. The y-axis represents "minADE₂₀ (←)", scaled linearly from 0.60 to 0.66, with tick marks at 0.61, 0.62, 0.63, 0.64, 0.65, and 0.66, indicating lower values are better. The blue line with circular markers, representing ST-ES, starts at a minADE₂₀ of approximately 0.66 when the number of examples is 0, drops sharply to about 0.60 at 1 example, then fluctuates slightly between 0.59 and 0.60 for higher numbers of examples, ending at approximately 0.59 at 8 examples. The orange line with circular markers, representing Random selection, remains relatively stable throughout, starting at approximately 0.64 at 0 examples and varying slightly between 0.63 and 0.64 up to 8 examples, ending at about 0.64. The ST-ES method consistently achieves lower minADE₂₀ values than the Random method across all numbers of examples shown.
model_annotations.German: The plot illustrates the performance of two methods—ST-ES (blue line with circular markers) and Random (orange line with circular markers)—in terms of minADE₂₀ (a metric for trajectory prediction accuracy) as the number of in-context examples varies from 0 to 8. The x-axis, labeled "Number of Examples," is linear and ranges from 0 to 8 with tick marks at integer intervals. The y-axis, labeled "minADE₂₀ (←)", is also linear and ranges from 0.60 to 0.66, with tick marks at 0.01 intervals. For the ST-ES method, the minADE₂₀ starts at 0.66 when no examples are provided, then drops sharply to 0.60 at 1 example, and remains relatively stable between 0.59 and 0.60 for 2 to 8 examples, with minor fluctuations. In contrast, the Random method begins at 0.64 with 0 examples, dips slightly to 0.63 at 2 examples, and then fluctuates between 0.63 and 0.64 for 2 to 8 examples, showing little improvement. The ST-ES method consistently achieves lower minADE₂₀ values than the Random method across all numbers of examples, indicating superior performance.
